images.title: Pieces of different sizes
images.purpose: Show that one 1/2 piece, one 1/4 piece and two 1/8 pieces make one whole, and that one 1/8 piece is covered by two 1/16 pieces.
images.composition: A whole circle made of a 1/2, a 1/4 and two 1/8 pieces on the left, and one enlarged 1/8 piece cut into two 1/16 parts on the right, joined by an arrow.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Thin dark #2B2B2B cut lines and outlines (3 px) throughout. LEFT: one whole circle, centre (380, 330), radius 220 (x 160 to 600, y 110 to 550), cut by radii into exactly 4 pieces, with angles counted clockwise from 12 o'clock: (1) one piece of 1/2, the left half, from 180 to 360 degrees, filled teal #0072B2, label 1/2 in white bold sans-serif (52 px) at its middle; (2) one piece of 1/4, the top right quarter, from 0 to 90 degrees, filled amber #E69F00, label 1/4 in dark #1F2937 bold (44 px); (3) one piece of 1/8 from 90 to 135 degrees and (4) one piece of 1/8 from 135 to 180 degrees, both filled reddish purple #CC79A7, each labelled 1/8 in dark bold (36 px). The 4 pieces fill the circle with no gap and no overlap. Under the circle, centred at x 380 and y 630, the line 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/8 = 1 in dark bold sans-serif (44 px). MIDDLE: one thin construction grey #6B7280 arrow (5 px) pointing right at y 414, from x 625 (just outside the 1/8 piece that runs from 90 to 135 degrees) to x 985, with a solid arrowhead. RIGHT: one enlarged piece of 1/8 drawn as a wedge of 45 degrees with its point at (1060, 570), radius 340, pointing up, so it spans about x 930 to 1190 and y 256 to 570; filled reddish purple #CC79A7 with the same outline. One solid dark line (3 px) from the point straight up cuts it into exactly 2 equal parts of 22.5 degrees, and each part carries the label 1/16 in dark bold sans-serif (30 px). Under the wedge, centred at x 1060 and y 660, the line 1/8 = 2/16 in dark bold (64 px), the largest text in the frame. No other text. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
pieces that overlap, leave a gap or do not add up to one whole circle
a circle cut into any pieces other than one 1/2, one 1/4 and two 1/8
images.takeaway: Pieces of different sizes can make a whole, and a piece can be covered by smaller equal pieces, which gives it a second name: 1/8 = 2/16.
images.description: A whole circle made of one 1/2, one 1/4 and two 1/8 pieces, and one 1/8 piece shown larger and cut into two 1/16 parts, with 1/8 = 2/16 written below.
images.context: Concept image for Making a Whole with Different Pieces. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (a whole made of a 1/2 piece and smaller pieces, a piece covered by two smaller ones) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and 1/16.
images.teaching_notes: Cover the 1/8 piece with the two 1/16 parts and ask how many of them fit. The slip to watch: calling the two parts 1/2 each, instead of naming them by how many of them fill the whole.

image_decisions.why: The circle of four different pieces and the enlarged 1/8 piece with its two 1/16 parts make the two names of one part visible.
